subject.title: Telegram: collapse mid-paragraph newlines before sending

question: Should Telegram collapse model-emitted single newlines inside prose/list items by default, expose an opt-in setting, or keep newline preservation as the supported behavior?
rationale: Current code and recent rich-message fixes intentionally preserve visible single newlines, while a safe collapse path likely needs either a public config knob or an explicit default-policy tradeoff.

options.title: Add Opt-In Collapse Policy
options.body: Add a Telegram config option for Markdown-aware soft-wrap collapse, default it off, and document/test preserved blocks plus rich/plain behavior.

options.title: Make Collapse Default
options.body: Change Telegram output globally to collapse detected soft wraps, accepting compatibility risk for users who rely on single-newline preservation.

options.title: Keep Preservation Behavior
options.body: Confirm preserving model newlines is the intended Telegram behavior and close this direction in favor of prompts or formatting guidance.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Collapse Policy
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram config option for Markdown-aware soft-wrap collapse, default it off, and document/test preserved blocks plus rich/plain behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the strongest recent ownership signal on the Telegram rich formatter and send boundary where this policy would be implemented.
